name: Wirewound resistor
note: Precision requires consistent wire diameter and tight winding; achromatic winding balances inductance.

name: Carbon composition resistor
note: Carbon content and binder ratio set resistance; tolerance broader than wirewound but adequate for most circuits.

name: Rheostat sliding contact resistor
note: Current path through coil via moving contact; heating limits power; precision determines smoothness.

name: Potentiometer precision voltage divider
note: Known voltage (from standard cell) balanced against unknown via null galvanometer. Sliding contact on calibrated wire determines ratio. Zero-current measurement avoids galvanic heating.

name: Fixed mica capacitor
note: A capacitor stores electric charge on two conducting plates separated by a thin insulator. In a mica capacitor the insulator is mica, a mineral that splits cleanly into very thin, even sheets, with metal foil or coating on each side. Its capacitance changes very little with temperature or age, so it is used where stability matters, as in radio and timing circuits. It needs a supply of good mica and care in cutting and stacking it.

name: Fixed paper capacitor
note: Oil impregnation lowers losses and increases voltage rating; absorbs water readily so must be sealed; cheap at scale.

name: Electrolytic capacitor aluminium
note: Oxide thickness controls voltage rating; only works in one polarity; sensitive to temperature and overvolts; vastly higher C/V than paper capacitors.

name: Variable air-gap capacitor
note: A variable capacitor has interleaved sets of metal plates with only air between them, one set fixed and the other turning on a shaft. Turning the shaft changes how much the plates overlap, and so changes the capacitance smoothly. This is how radio sets are tuned to a station. Air cannot be permanently damaged by a spark, so arcing does no lasting harm. It needs well-fitted plates and a smooth-running bearing, and the metal leads add small unwanted effects at radio frequencies.

name: Air-core inductor coil
note: Inductance scales as turns squared; skin effect at high frequency; useful where DC or variable core losses unacceptable.

name: Iron-core inductor and choke
note: Saturation nonlinearity used for current limiting; core loss scales with frequency; permeability much higher than air.

name: Ferrite and powdered iron core
note: Ferrite a ceramic; does not conduct eddy currents like iron sheet; high frequency inductor and transformer cores.

name: Quartz resonator and filter
note: Mechanical resonance; Q can exceed 10000; temperature coefficient critical; must be mounted to damp overtones without killing Q.

name: Electromagnetic relay switching contacts
note: Arc damage and pitting of contacts with AC load; silvering extends life; must account for contact resistance in design.

name: Industrial contactor and motor starter
note: Arc chute prevents sustained arc; overload heater coil; three-phase main contacts plus auxiliary; frame standardization aids design.

name: Knife switch and disconnect
note: No arc suppression; safe only at voltages below 600V or in oil bath; contact pressure from spring determines resistance.

name: Thermal circuit breaker
note: Time-current characteristic depends on heater coil; not fast; reset after cooling; can be overridden by sustained high current.

name: Magnetic circuit breaker fast trip
note: Can be combined with thermal for dual protection; must dissipate solenoid heat continuously; coordination between devices essential.

name: Fuse and wire element cartridge
kb: Fusible element melts at predetermined current, breaking circuit
note: Melt point set by wire diameter and alloy; cartridge design isolates arc; single-use requires replacement; cost nearly zero.

name: Lightning arrestor and gap protector
note: Horn gap spreads arc to cool it; prevents sustained arc-over; must be coordinated with fuse or breaker to isolate line if arc grounds.

name: Porcelain pin insulator
note: Creepage distance (surface path) more critical than straight-line distance; pollution tracking and salt spray demand careful glaze design.

name: Oil-filled bushing insulator transformer
note: Stress grading with increasing porcelain thickness reduces field; oil cooling improves thermal rating; must handle thermal cycling without cracking.

name: Portable electrical plug and socket
note: Keying and grounding contacts critical; contact wear and oxidation cause heating; standardization enables interoperability.

name: Printed circuit board etched pattern
note: Etching must be selective and reproducible; copper adhesion critical; allows mass assembly; enables high-density interconnect.

name: Air-gap transformer inductive coupling
note: Loose coupling limits power transfer; useful for RF and signalling; avoids eddy loss but requires many turns.

name: Shunt-wound dynamo generator
note: Self-exciting; voltage drops with load; external load variation affects output; inherently stable at constant speed.

name: Series-wound dynamo generator
note: Voltage rises with load if load resistance drops; dangerous behavior if load suddenly disconnected; stabilised by armature reaction.

name: Compound-wound dynamo self-regulating
note: Over-compound raises voltage with load; under-compound drops voltage; exact balance requires field connection points adjustment.

name: Alternator with rotating magnetic field
note: Slip rings carry small DC to field; no commutator means no brush wear on power output; AC frequency locks to mechanical speed.

name: Synchronous motor locked to line frequency
note: Must be brought up to speed by starting cage winding; field not self-excited; can operate at leading power factor and improve system power factor.

name: Squirrel-cage induction motor
note: Torque from electromagnetic induction in rotor; starting current high; rotor skew reduces cogging torque; slot geometry critical for performance.

name: Wound-rotor induction motor adjustable speed
note: Resistor heat at reduced speed; used for high-inertia loads; speed varies with load but controlled resistance keeps current safe.

name: Universal motor AC and DC rated
note: Commutation challenges at 50-60 Hz on AC; brush wear in higher air-gap flux field limits life; small portable motors favour this design.

name: Permanent magnet stepper motor
note: Precise repeatable positioning; holding torque when de-energised; microstepping smooth motion at cost of torque; frequency response limited by inductance.

name: Servo motor with feedback control
note: Feedback must have minimum lag; damping by proportional term prevents oscillation; used in remote positioning and radar antenna drives.

name: Rotary converter and synchronous converter AC-DC
kb: Combined induction motor stator and DC dynamo rotor; converts AC power to DC
note: Synchronous tie to AC line frequency; commutator ripple frequency same as AC frequency; largely replaced by mercury arc rectifier.

name: Mercury arc rectifier thermionic
note: Starting requires heated filament or external ignition; arc extinction requires current reversal; phase-shift transformer enables delay control.

name: Metal layer rectifier selenium or copper oxide
note: Forward voltage drop higher than tube; efficiency adequate for small rectifiers; stack many discs for high voltage; temperature coefficient positive.

name: Electrodynamometer and wattmeter

name: AC impedance bridge and LCR bridge
note: Accuracy depends on standard elements; frequency dependent; Q measurement by additional measurement or by ratio of R and L.

name: Weston standard cell voltage reference
note: Shielded from light and vibration; electrodes in saturated sulfate solution; used to calibrate voltmeters; temperature coefficient -0.0000406V/K.

name: Standard resistor manganin coil
note: Calibrated against international standard; typical accuracy 0.01%; stored in constant-temperature enclosure.

name: Potentiometer method voltage comparison
note: No current drawn from unknown source; used to compare EMFs and measure internal resistance; accuracy limited by potentiometer linearity.

name: Ballistic galvanometer pulse integration
note: Must measure total swing angle; temperature coefficient of spring critical; used to measure transformer turns ratio and core losses.

name: Oscillograph string galvanometer pen recorder
note: DC coupled; bandwidth limited by string inertia; essential for transient and power system measurements; requires continuous paper supply.

name: Cathode ray oscilloscope CRO
note: First practical CRO circa 1930s; sweep generator must have linear time base; persistence of phosphor crucial for observation.

name: Thermionic valve voltmeter high impedance
note: Measures voltage without loading circuit; DC-coupled version drifts; AC-coupled for AC signals; useful for high-impedance transducers.

name: Diode thermionic tube rectifier
note: Soft vacuum has gas ionisation current; hard vacuum preferred; anode heat limits rectification current; used in high-frequency radio reception.

name: Klystron microwave amplifier and oscillator
note: A klystron is a vacuum tube that amplifies or generates microwaves. A beam of electrons is sent through a hollow metal chamber called a cavity, where the signal speeds some electrons and slows others, so they bunch up as they travel on. The bunches then give up energy to a second cavity, which delivers a much stronger signal. The cavity size sets the frequency. It needs a good vacuum and precise copper cavities, and it was used in radar transmitters.

name: Tuned circuit resonance tank LC
note: An inductor (coil) and capacitor in series, tuned so that capacitive and inductive reactances cancel at a chosen frequency. At resonance, the impedance is minimum (current maximum), and the circuit selects only that frequency, rejecting others. This is THE solution to radio crowding: without tuning, all radio stations interfere. With tuning, each receiver selects one station and rejects the rest. Frequency = 1/(2*pi*sqrt(L*C)). A variable capacitor lets listeners tune across the band.

name: Resonance and Q factor frequency selectivity
note: Energy storage in L and C reactances Q times energy dissipated per cycle; Q limited by resistance in practical circuits.

name: RC low-pass and high-pass filters
note: Low-pass blocks high frequencies; high-pass blocks low frequencies; cutoff at -3dB point where reactance equals resistance.

name: Band-pass and notch filters tuned rejection
note: Bandwidth depends on Q of tuned circuit; notch depth limited by element losses; used for interference rejection in radio.

name: Amplifier stage and gain
note: Amplification occurs because small grid voltage controls large plate current; coupling network isolates stages and blocks DC.

name: Negative feedback and Blacks 1927 theorem
note: Black's insight 1927: gain with feedback equals open-loop gain divided by (1 + loop gain); distortion reduced by same factor.

name: Oscillator feedback oscillation and frequency generation
note: Starting from thermal noise; loop gain must exceed unity; crystal oscillator very stable; LC oscillator easily variable frequency.

name: Multivibrator astable and monostable binary circuit
note: Astable multivibrator: relaxation oscillator; monostable: one stable state, pulse triggered; chain of multivibrators forms binary counter.

name: Flip-flop latch and binary memory element
note: SR and JK flip-flops used for sequential logic; race conditions when setting and resetting simultaneously; trigger must be brief.

name: Counter frequency division and binary scaling
note: Used in frequency meters and timers; ripple counter has propagation delay; synchronous counter uses common clock.

name: Mixer frequency conversion and translation
note: Heterodyne conversion; intermediate frequency allows fixed narrowband amplification; mixer loss adds noise figure.

name: Detector and demodulation envelope and product detection
note: Rectifier bias sets detection point; high load resistance needed for AM; product detection with local oscillator restores suppressed carrier.

name: Discriminator and FM demodulation
note: S-curve characteristic; slope at center provides deviation sensitivity; FM less noise-prone than AM for same bandwidth.

name: Modulator amplitude frequency and phase modulation
note: AM needs linear amplification; FM needs frequency-stable oscillator; deviation ratio determines bandwidth.

name: Power supply rectification and smoothing
note: Capacitor input filter: ripple voltage decreases with size; inductor input: smoother initial voltage rise; transformer secondary voltage higher for same DC.

note: Bandwidth limited for transformer; L-network single frequency; Smith chart aids design; unnecessary if source and load both 50 ohm.

name: Transmission line and coaxial cable propagation
note: Velocity factor less than speed of light; skin effect increases loss at high frequency; wavelength determines physical line length.

name: Waveguide rectangular and circular propagation
note: Cutoff frequency below which wave does not propagate; multiple modes possible; mode matching required at junctions.

name: Antenna patterns radiation and efficiency gain
note: Radiation resistance determines efficiency; pattern directivity increases gain; matching network tunes reactance to resonance.

name: Arc welding carbon and metal electrode
note: AC welding problematic due to arc extinction each half-cycle; carbon electrode leaves residue; metal electrode suited to steel joining.

name: Radar pulse modulation and detection

name: Sonar acoustic detection and ranging
